verdicts.reason: The finite-tensor zig-zag argument excludes duals for k[x]. Both super-vector-space twists satisfy the ribbon axioms, and the Drinfeld and trace computations correctly give odd-line values -1 and 1, consistent with the supplied interfaces.

The incidence model verifies projectivity, and the cited interfaces supply smoothness and the exceptional fibre. Since [p]=[q] but proper pushforward sends their preimage cycles to 0 and [q] of degree 1, the recipe cannot descend.

Properness supplies extensions at vertical height-one points, finite-presentation descent spreads them, and separatedness permits gluing on an S-dense open. The resulting S-rational map satisfies the supplied Weil extension theorem's hypotheses.

The cited theorem applies to every abelian scheme model supplied by good reduction. The mapping property gives the stated uniqueness, and properness and smoothness follow from being an abelian scheme; the DVR specialization is valid.

Bezout supplies a finite intersection with total multiplicity df; positivity bounds its number of distinct points by df. The subset bound and common-component contrapositive follow, with hypotheses and dependency restatements consistent.

The coefficient expansion and Peter–Weyl orthogonality are correct. Compact-uniform approximation on K forces a nonzero pairing, excluding every inequivalent irreducible class and making each singleton Fell-open. Dependency interfaces are consistent.

The axioms, dual reflection action, bases, and contravariant lattice map in an isomorphism are consistent. Finiteness of W supplies an invariant inner product, and no dependency is inaccurately restated.

The gcd construction and unit ambiguity are valid, including the zero ideal. The recorded square-presentation and knot-normalisation facts support F3, and the E0 indexing and piecewise definition of D_L agree with the supplied interfaces.

The definitions and dependency restatements are consistent. The locally finite convention ensures closed supports and finite restrictions to quasi-compact opens; for finite type schemes it agrees with the displayed free abelian cycle groups.

No fatal defect found. Dependency restatements and constructions are consistent; the locally finite and birational equality tests agree with [Stacks, Lemma 42.35.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02UC).

Condition (iv) quantifies over all étale X'→X, but canonical resolutions are defined only for finite-type sources. For nonempty X, the étale map ⨿_{n∈ℕ}X→X has non-quasi-compact source, so its canonical resolution is outside this definition.

The descent proof correctly establishes categorical universality from (i)–(iii). Dependency restatements, uniqueness, the empty case, and the classical affine-model convention are consistent with the supplied interfaces.

The claimed well-definedness invokes lem-geometric-intersection-numbers-are-isotopy-invariants unconditionally, but its supplied interface assumes AC. This item never assumes AC, so the cited result does not license its unconditional independence claim.

The coefficient-witness refinement proves the basis axioms, and finite-sum tests yield the same topology. The definition is invariant under unitary equivalence and matches the supplied weak-containment and unitary-dual interfaces.
The definitions are well-defined with the component exclusions. The contact-order identities, finite-contact remarks and degree bounds agree with the supplied dependency interfaces.

The claim that the orbit-space assertion holds only on the stable locus is false. Let G=G_m act trivially on a point with trivial ample linearization. The semistable locus is the point and the stable locus is empty, yet its quotient is geometric.
The group-object axioms, functor-of-points equivalences, subgroup and kernel constructions, and base-change assertions are sound and consistent with the supplied dependency interfaces.
Definitions, dependency uses and A/B interfaces are consistent. The nilpotent-base size argument is sound; affineness follows from [Stacks Lemma 37.2.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04EW).

The invariant ring is graded by the cited equivariant section-ring lemma, Proj and its charts are defined without finite generation, and positive tensor powers give the stated Veronese invariance. The remarks agree with the supplied interfaces.

The observables are well-defined real random variables, including when n<k; joint convergence and Gaussian normalization agree with the supplied dependency and theorem interfaces. No fatal defect found.

The tensor construction, termwise Koszul reduction, induced differential and grading claims follow from the supplied interfaces. Finite-dimensional graded pieces and the exceptional empty-diagram a-action are handled correctly; no fatal defect found.

The path-span argument, computations of J² and J³, and explicit quotient isomorphism are valid, including m=1. Dependency restatements match the supplied interfaces, and no relevant A/B inconsistency appears.

The maximal-order criterion matches the dependency's characteristic hypotheses. Support containment follows from the all-characteristic derivative inclusion; multiplicity one and independent boundary classes give the stated regularity and transversality.

The model-category axioms and Quillen definitions are consistent. The left/right preservation equivalence follows from adjunction and the standard retract characterization of lifting classes; no fatal defect or inaccurate dependency restatement was found.

The controlled transform and boundary update are consistent with the supplied interfaces, including Cartier-center blowups and inserted isomorphisms. The resolution and extension definitions introduce no unsupported existence claim or fatal edge-case defect.

The dilatation universal property, differential criterion, defect formula, and uniform bound are valid. The cited interfaces support the argument together with routine local algebra; no fatal defect found.

The rigidity, Kunneth vanishing, finite-support Leray argument, and descent are sound. Factoring through the open Picard identity component also handles nonreduced tests.

No fatal defect found. The filtration, graph/DVR and étale-spreading arguments are sound under the supplied interfaces; compare [BLR §3.5](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf).

The title claims cross-sections for closed subgroups of all second-countable groups, but the statement and proof require local compactness and Hausdorffness. The title therefore asserts more than the proof establishes.

The projection case uses a valid induction on the base dimension, with coefficient and homogenization operations applied to maximal-order inputs. Étale functoriality then gives the smooth case through local factorization.

The componentwise field argument and connected intersection graph establish the single closed-point image. The affine conclusion follows from reducedness and the one-point spectrum. Dependency restatements and applications are consistent.

The contractibility hypothesis makes the augmented representable columns acyclic; exact evaluation gives acyclic augmented rows. Finite-diagonal elimination proves both roof maps are quasi-isomorphisms, and projective comparison gives independence and naturality.

The order-lowering inclusion, perfect-field Taylor detection, and factorial arguments are valid. Faithful flatness transfers the completed-local conclusions to stalks. Dependencies, edge cases, and A/B interfaces are consistent.

The chart calculation makes the lifted derivations regular and logarithmic along D. Leibniz proves the one-step inclusion, and admissibility of derivative centers plus monotonicity completes the induction, including r=0 and r=mu.

The root and coroot correspondence correctly preserves dominance under the central isogeny. The supplied product, primitive-vector quotient and descent interfaces then yield the claimed simple finite-dimensional module.

Step 6.1 invokes the fixed-coordinate formal-arc lemma, which requires an equicharacteristic starting ring. The statement does not assume equicharacteristic, and no prior step establishes it; thus the cited lemma does not license the termination argument.

The proof correctly separates matching companion passes from passes missed by a nonsurjective étale image. Order preservation, maximal-order functoriality, and the monomial boundary data justify the centers and invariant comparisons.

The neighbourhood criterion matches the supplied Fell basis, and its quantifiers agree exactly with weak containment. The finite-sum approximation argument is valid, and the statement and title follow.

The family-selection interface licenses the simultaneous approximation in step 2.1, yielding the claimed neighbourhood basis. Step 3.1 correctly normalizes and rescales nonzero coefficients and handles zero vectors. No fatal defect found.

Step 2.1 claims AC enters only through the lifting facts, but steps 1.2 and 2.1 also invoke F2–F4, whose supplied dependency interfaces explicitly assume AC. The proof does not justify this claimed restriction of AC use.

Smoothness upgrades H(k)-fixing to scheme-theoretic stabilizer inclusion. Normality fixes the orbit morphism, and schematic dominance preserved under products over k extends stability and triviality to its reduced closure. Dependency restatements are accurate.

The dimension argument, local prime-filtration and length calculations, descent, functoriality, and localization are valid under the supplied interfaces and locally finite cycle conventions. No fatal defect found.

The relative comparison matches [Khovanov–Seidel, Lemmas 3.2–3.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0006056). Simultaneous transport and the boundary collar correction establish invariance; no fatal defect or interface conflict found.

Base change follows from the cited stability lemma. The number-field spreading argument satisfies the stage and cohomology hypotheses; clearing finitely many denominators preserves the group laws, smoothness, and geometrically connected fibres.

The localized Reynolds map is well defined, and the G-stable complement to f-torsion supplies invariant numerators without a domain hypothesis. The grading argument and degree-zero conclusion are valid, including zero or nilpotent f, and consistent with the supplied interfaces.

The Koszul induction, Tor-vanishing restriction argument, and deformation-fibre application are sound. The dependency restatements match the supplied interfaces, and the stated hypotheses cover the required exactness.

The mapping-property arguments, finite-stage descent, and gluing are valid under the stated hypotheses. Dependency restatements are consistent, and separatedness with flatness justifies uniqueness from agreement on the generic fibre.

Step 5.1 invokes F5, which requires an equicharacteristic starting ring. The stated hypotheses neither assert nor establish this condition; normal completion does not imply it. Thus the formal-arc construction is not licensed by the cited interface.

The normality argument, Leray five-term sequence, finite-support sheaf argument, and projective H² vanishing are valid and licensed by the supplied dependencies; no fatal defect found.

The coproduct construction, representable etale cover, and gluing of scheme-valued equality functors establish the claims. Dependency restatements are accurate, and arbitrary families and empty cases cause no defect.

No fatal defect found. Projective-bundle uniqueness, Cartier compatibility, flag-tower descent and the rank-zero case are sound. The section induction agrees with [Stacks §42.44](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0FA8).

No fatal defect found. The proof steps and dependency restatements are valid, including arbitrary-field descent, nonreduced centres, finite intersections, and the quotient and product assertions.

The exact identity, overlap classification and coefficient count are valid and agree with [Ivanov–Olshanski, Props. 4.11–4.12](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0304010). Edge cases and the distinct filtrations are handled consistently.

The generic-point DVR argument makes H nonzero; nonzeros give regular successors, simple zeros give nonsquare tangent quadratics, and degree three allows at most one multiple closed zero, necessarily rational. Dependency restatements and uses are consistent.

The finite affine Čech complexes identify under base change, and flat tensoring commutes with their cohomology. The dependency interfaces support the argument; no flatness of F is needed, and the empty-scheme case is valid.

The derivative-transform inclusion and chart calculations establish support containment, including equal-support and Cartier centers. Initial boundary transversality permits compatible center parameters and validates the restricted blow-up sequence.

Bezout supplies a finite intersection sum equal to the degree product, and positivity bounds the number of distinct intersection points. Both equal-degree and degree-bounded formulations follow; dependency restatements and hypotheses are consistent.

The closed-orbit and stable affine-chart arguments establish both intersection identities; the centralizer and fixed-subgroup consequences follow. Dependency restatements and scheme-theoretic hypotheses are consistent with the supplied interfaces.

The splitting, explicit inverse operator rules, normalization comparisons, and exactness argument are sound. Dependency restatements match the supplied interfaces; degree-zero conventions and constant-ring scope are consistent.

The pointed torsor classification from [Stacks 08UZ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08UZ) applies correctly. The scheme, flatness and finite-presentation arguments cover arbitrary I; dependency restatements and A/B interfaces are consistent.

The cited interfaces license the construction and translation extensions. Finite-stage spreading covers all vertical height-one points; Weil extension and faithful-flat descent then establish the mapping property and uniqueness.

The controlled-transform factorization proves principalization; the intrinsic-constant-field argument validly reduces arbitrary ideal-preserving automorphisms to the cited semilinear comparison. No fatal defect found.

The free-diagram and free-section adjunctions justify the lifting classes and small-object constructions. Extension of scalars preserves acyclic cofibrations, and the cotensor corners and cone adjunction satisfy the required simplicial and Quillen properties.

The closure identity follows from the supplied family-selection lemma and kernel-inclusion theorem. All dependency restatements agree with their interfaces, and the continuity, closedness, quotient argument, and empty-set case are valid.

The intersection series is scheme-theoretically central; each quotient is its closed image in G_a by the cited kernel-quotient theorem. The lower central and derived series terminate, including for nonreduced groups and the n=1 edge case. Dependency restatements are consistent.

[F2] inaccurately restates its cited interfaces: neither the maximal-torus lemma nor the conjugacy theorem asserts Borel existence or splitness over k. The conjugacy theorem also requires k algebraically closed, a hypothesis omitted in [F2].
